# Manage self-managed static roles in the Vault GUI

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

Use the Vault GUI to create, view, and edit
[self-managed static roles](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap#static-roles) for the LDAP
secrets engine. A self-managed static role rotates its own LDAP password, so
Vault does not need an administrator bind account with elevated permissions.
You give Vault the account's current password when you create the role, and
Vault uses that password to manage future rotations.

The GUI adapts the role pages to the mode of the LDAP mount:

- **Create** shows only the fields the mount accepts. On a self-managed mount,
  the form goes straight to a static role and requires the distinguished name
  (DN) and the current password.
- **Edit** keeps the stored password unless you explicitly replace it.
- **Details** and **Get credentials** mask the password, and show it only to
  users who can read the role's credentials.
- **Restricted tokens** that cannot read the mount configuration see a warning
  that the mode is unknown. **Create role** appears only for users who can
  create roles.

## Before you start

- **Use Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 or later**. Self-managed static roles and the
  `self_managed` mount setting are Enterprise features. GUI support for
  self-managed static roles starts in Vault Enterprise 2.2.0.

- **Configure a self-managed LDAP secrets engine**. Set `self_managed=true`
  when you first configure the mount with the CLI or API. The GUI configuration
  form does not include this setting, and you cannot change it after you
  configure the mount. Do not set `bindpass` on a self-managed mount, because
  Vault rejects the configuration. For example:

  ```shell-session
  $ vault secrets enable -path=self-managed-ldap ldap
  $ vault write self-managed-ldap/config \
      url="ldaps://ldap.example.com" \
      schema="openldap" \
      self_managed=true
  ```

- **Check your permissions**. Your policy must grant the capabilities for the
  actions you want to perform:

  | GUI action | Path | Capability |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Detect the self-managed mode | `<mount>/config` | `read` |
  | Display and use **Create role** | A path beneath `<mount>/static-role/` | `create` |
  | View role details | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `read` |
  | Edit a role | `<mount>/static-role/<name>` | `update` |
  | Display the **Password** row and **Get credentials** | `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` | `read` |
  | Rotate credentials manually | `<mount>/rotate-role/<name>` | `update` |

  The following policy lets a user manage self-managed static roles and view
  their credentials:

  ```hcl
  path "self-managed-ldap/config"         { capabilities = ["read"] }
  path "self-managed-ldap/static-role/*"  { capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "list"] }
  path "self-managed-ldap/static-cred/*"  { capabilities = ["read"] }
  path "self-managed-ldap/rotate-role/*"  { capabilities = ["update"] }
  ```

## Step 1: Create a self-managed static role

1. Open the Vault GUI, go to **Secrets engines**, and select your self-managed
   LDAP mount.

1. Open the **Roles** tab and click **Create role**. The **Create static role**
   form opens. Self-managed mounts support only static roles, so the form does
   not show the **Static role** and **Dynamic role** options or any dynamic
   role fields.

1. Complete the fields:

   | Field | Required | Description |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Role name | Yes | The name of the role in Vault. Use lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens (`-`), underscores (`_`), periods (`.`), and forward slashes (`/`). You cannot rename a role after you create it. |
   | Distinguished name | Yes | The DN of the existing LDAP entry, for example `cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com`. You cannot change the DN after you create the role. |
   | Username | Yes | The username of the existing LDAP entry to manage. |
   | Password | Yes | The current LDAP password for the account. The GUI masks the value as you type. Vault uses the password to manage future rotations. |
   | Rotation period | No | How often Vault rotates the password. The default is `0`, which turns off automatic rotation. |

1. Click **Create role**. Vault creates the role and opens its details page.

The GUI checks the form before it sends a request to Vault. If a field is empty
or invalid, Vault receives no request and the form shows a message under the
field:

| Field | Message |
| --- | --- |
| Role name | `Role name is required`, or `Name must be lowercase and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, periods, and forward slashes.` |
| Distinguished name | `Enter the distinguished name (DN) of the LDAP account` |
| Username | `Enter the username of the LDAP account` |
| Password | `Enter the current password for this LDAP account` |
| Rotation period | `Rotation period is too large. Maximum allowed value is 106,751 days.` |

The rotation period controls automatic rotation:

- A value of `0` turns off automatic rotation. You can still rotate the
  password on demand from **Manage** > **Rotate credentials** if your policy
  grants `update` on `<mount>/rotate-role/<name>`.
- Any other value rotates the password at that interval. Choose seconds,
  minutes, hours, or days, up to a maximum of 106,751 days.
- The rotation period is optional. The GUI saves an empty value as `0`, so an
  empty field never blocks submission.

Creating the role in the GUI produces the same role as the following CLI
command:

```shell-session
$ vault write self-managed-ldap/static-role/billing-svc \
    dn="cn=billing-svc,ou=services,dc=example,dc=com" \
    username="billing-svc" \
    password="<current-password>" \
    rotation_period=0
```

## Step 2: View the role password

The details page masks the **Password** row by default. Vault sends the
password to the browser only when you ask to see it.

1. Open the role from the **Roles** tab.

1. In the **Password** row, click the eye icon to show the value. The GUI reads
   `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` and displays the password. Click the copy icon
   to copy it.

The displayed value matches the `password` field that the CLI returns:

```shell-session
$ vault read self-managed-ldap/static-cred/billing-svc
```

The **Password** row appears for root-managed and self-managed static roles,
when your policy lets you read the role's credentials. Refer to
[Permissions and the password field](#permissions-and-the-password-field) for
details.

## Step 3: Get the role credentials

Click **Get credentials** on the role details page to open the credentials page
for the static credential that Vault manages:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Last Vault rotation | When Vault last rotated the password. Displays `Never` if Vault has not rotated it, for example a role with a rotation period of `0` that nobody rotated manually. |
| Password | The current password, masked by default, with show value and copy icons. |
| Username | The LDAP username. |
| Rotation period | The configured rotation period. `0` means automatic rotation is off. |
| Time remaining | The time until the next automatic rotation. `0` when automatic rotation is off. |

<Note>

Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 and 2.2.1 display a placeholder date in the year 0001
instead of `Never` for roles that Vault has not rotated. Vault Enterprise 2.2.2
and later display `Never`.

</Note>

## Step 4: Edit the role

1. Open the role details page.

1. Click **Manage**, then **Edit role**. The **Edit Role** page shows the same
   fields as the create form for the mount's mode.

1. Update the fields you want to change. **Role name** and
   **Distinguished name** are read-only. Vault does not let you change the
   username after you create the role, so keep the existing value.

1. Choose how to handle the password:

   - To keep the current password, leave the **Password** field locked.
   - To set a new password, click **Enable input**, then enter the new
     password.

1. Click **Save**.

Vault never sends the stored password to the edit form, so the field is empty
after you click **Enable input**. The password is optional when you edit a
role. If you leave the field empty, Vault keeps the existing password. You
cannot lock the field again after you enable it. If you enable it by mistake,
leave it empty and save, or click **Cancel**.

Editing works the same way on root-managed mounts. The edit form displays the
**Static role** and **Dynamic role** options but disables them, because you
cannot change a static role to a dynamic role, or a dynamic role to a static
role.

## Compare self-managed and root-managed mounts

The GUI reads the `self_managed` setting from `<mount>/config` and displays the
matching form. Root-managed mounts keep the standard form, with an optional
password field.

| | Root-managed (`self_managed=false`) | Self-managed (`self_managed=true`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who rotates passwords | Vault, using the mount's bind account | Vault, using each role's own password |
| Role types | Static and dynamic | Static only |
| Create page title | **Create Role** | **Create static role** |
| **Static role** and **Dynamic role** options | Displayed | Hidden |
| Distinguished name | Optional | Required, and you cannot change it after creation |
| Username | Required | Required |
| Password | Optional | Required |
| Rotation period | Optional, defaults to `0` | Optional, defaults to `0` |

## Permissions and the password field

The GUI shows credentials only to users who can read them. If your policy does
not grant `read` on `<mount>/static-cred/<name>`:

- The details page does not display the **Password** row.
- The details page does not display the **Get credentials** button.

This behavior applies to static roles on root-managed and self-managed mounts.

## Create roles without permission to read the mount configuration

The GUI determines whether a mount is self-managed by reading `<mount>/config`.
Vault returns the `self_managed` setting only from that path. If your policy
denies the read and Vault returns a `403` error, the GUI cannot tell which mode
the mount uses.

In that case, the create page:

- Displays the warning **Unable to determine LDAP configuration mode**. The
  warning explains that self-managed engines do not support dynamic roles and
  require a password and DN for static roles.
- Uses the standard form, with the **Static role** and **Dynamic role** options
  and without required badges on the DN or password, because the GUI cannot
  assume either mode.

When you submit the form, Vault applies the mount's own rules. On a
self-managed mount, Vault rejects a role without a DN or password, and the form
displays a Vault error that names the missing field, such as
`dn is a required field for a self-managed static role` or
`password is a required field for a self-managed static role`. Add the missing
value and click **Create role** again.

<Tip>

To give role creators the full self-managed form, grant `read` on
`<mount>/config`. The GUI then hides the **Static role** and **Dynamic role**
options and checks the DN and password before it submits the form.

</Tip>

## Create role visibility

The GUI offers a way to create roles only to users whose policy lets them
create one. If your policy does not allow it, the GUI hides:

- The **Create role** button on the **Roles** tab.
- The **Create new** link on the **Roles** card of the **Overview** page.

Users who can only read or list roles can still browse them. The GUI hides
these options so that it does not open a form that the user cannot submit.

The capability your policy needs depends on the type of mount:

| Mount | Your policy needs `create` on |
| --- | --- |
| Self-managed | Any path under `<mount>/static-role/`, because self-managed mounts support only static roles |
| Root-managed | Any path under `<mount>/static-role/` or `<mount>/role/` |
| Unknown, because your policy cannot read `<mount>/config` | Any path under `<mount>/static-role/` or `<mount>/role/` |

The path can be narrower than the whole folder. For example, a policy that
grants `create` on `self-managed-ldap/static-role/team-*` is enough to display
**Create role**.

## Limitations

- You must set the `self_managed` mode with the CLI or API when you configure
  the mount. The GUI configuration form does not include it.
- The role form covers **Role name**, **Distinguished name**, **Username**,
  **Password**, and **Rotation period**. To set other static role parameters,
  such as `password_policy`, `rotation_schedule`, `rotation_window`, or
  `rotation_policy`, use the CLI or API.
